about: What stands under the bridges that have no model of their own (owner, 27 Nov 2026: 'where are the legs of the bridge?', 'bridge is floating'). The three railway viaducts are in viaducts.json. Every other bridge of the transport graph gets stone arches on piers by the rule in 'supports' (the owner chose arches over plain piers from samples, 27 Nov 2026). A bridge named in 'frames' is modelled by hand instead. Every number not from a source is marked as an assumption. Spec: v2/docs/specs/structures.md. Checked by check_structures.

supports.about: OpenStreetMap does not say what most bridges are made of, so one rule serves all: round stone arches on piers, the span following the height.

deck_thickness_m.note: the slab layer 6 draws under every bridge way

min_clear_m.assumption: a deck less than this over the ground has no opening: its sides go down to the ground

min_open_m.assumption: a stretch shorter than this that stands clear gets no arch (its sides go down to the ground)

span_per_height.assumption: masonry viaducts of the city: 15 m arches at 30-45 m (Clausen, Pfaffenthal)

span_m.assumption: the least and the largest arch

pier_per_span.assumption: pier thickness along the deck as a share of the span

pier_m.assumption: the thinnest and the thickest pier

crown_m.assumption: stone between the arch's crown and the slab

rise_share.assumption: a low arch rises over this share of the room under its crown (a round arch where there is room for one)

parallel_gap_m.assumption: ways of one bridge (a road and its footways, two tracks) run within this of each other: they share one row of arches

way_margin_m.assumption: room kept between a pier and a road, track or path passing under the bridge

frames.name: Grand Duchess Charlotte Bridge (Pont Grande-Duchesse Charlotte, Roud Bréck)
frames.structure: strut frame: a steel box girder on two pairs of slanted legs

feet_apart_m.assumption: the main span as remembered (355 m long, 234 m main span); not checked against a source

leg_run_per_height.assumption: how far a leg leans toward the middle per metre it rises; read off research/01-landmarks/images/red-bridge__aerial.jpg and red-bridge__exterior.jpg

haunch_m.assumption: the girder is deeper over the legs by this much; to verify on photos

girder_width_share.assumption: the girder's width as a share of the deck's (the footways overhang); read off the aerial photo

leg_offset_share.assumption: each leg's place across the deck, either side of the axis, as a share of the deck's width

leg_top_m.assumption: a leg's size at the girder, along and across the bridge

leg_foot_m.assumption: a leg's size at its foot: the legs taper (the aerial photo)

footing_m.assumption: a concrete block under each foot: along, across, height

sources: OpenStreetMap ways named Pont Grande-Duchesse Charlotte
